available.title: Automatic encrypted backup
available.description: Every ~30 seconds, new or changed files in your backup folder are encrypted on your device and sent to your buddy. Deleting a file locally removes it from your buddy's live copy too (older versions stay recoverable for 30 days). Large files (up to 1 TB each) and large folders are handled in steady, low memory, and unchanged files are never re-read.

available.title: Encrypted file and folder names
available.description: Since client 0.14.0, your buddy can't see what your files or folders are called: every name is encrypted on your device, the way rclone's crypt does it, and your passphrase brings the names back on restore. Updating re-sends what's already backed up once, under the new names. Names over 127 bytes can't be backed up and are flagged on your dashboard. What your buddy can still see: file sizes, how many files you have, how your folders nest and how many entries each holds, and when things change.

available.title: See what your buddy sees
available.description: Since client 0.15.0, Browse files has a “What your buddy sees” view: your files listed the way they sit on your buddy's disk, with encrypted names and stored sizes, and the first bytes of any one exactly as stored (an age header, then ciphertext). You can check for yourself that nothing on their side is readable, instead of taking our word for it.

available.title: Direct peer-to-peer transfer, with automatic relay fallback
available.description: Your device and your buddy's device try to connect directly first. On the same local network, that's instant and automatic. Over the internet, it depends on both sides' network and router. When a direct connection isn't possible, your data still transfers reliably through our relay, which can never read it (see “Known limitations” below for when this applies).

available.title: Restore, including file history
available.description: Restore a single file, restore everything your buddy has for you at once, or pull back a specific earlier version of a file you've since changed or deleted (kept for 30 days, or remove a deleted file's copies sooner with “Delete permanently”), with a live progress indicator while it runs.

available.title: Pledge-based storage limits
available.description: Each buddy pairing has an agreed storage size. Going over it is refused automatically, and your dashboard tells you exactly why a file didn't send (pledge full, file too large, buddy's disk full).

available.title: More than one buddy
available.description: You can pair with as many buddies as you like, through invite codes or Find a buddy. Each pairing is its own 1:1 pledge, and your backup folder goes to every buddy, so each one holds its own full encrypted copy. Your pledges add up toward the 50GB free tier, and your disk needs room for everything you've pledged (the dashboard warns you if it doesn't have it).

available.title: Drift detection (reconciliation)
available.description: Roughly every 10 minutes, your device double-checks that what your buddy actually has on disk still matches what it expects, catching anything lost or changed outside the normal backup flow, and automatically re-sends anything missing.

available.title: Unreachable-buddy detection
available.description: If your buddy's device genuinely can't be reached, your dashboard flags it as stale rather than silently showing “backup ok”. It's backed by a real connectivity check, not an assumption.

available.title: Dashboard
available.description: Per-buddy backup status (with a live progress bar, speed and time left while a backup is running), your device's name/build/uptime/local file count, how many buddies are currently visible on your local network, each buddy's real disk usage, a lifetime direct-vs-relay bandwidth breakdown, an Activity log, the exclude list, and a warning for big files that keep re-sending. Behind its own login.

available.title: Find a buddy
available.description: Browse public listings at an exact storage size, and narrow them by country and minimum upload speed (10 or 50 Mbps and up). Listings also show self-reported “usually online” and “relay-only” info, to help you judge fit before pairing.

available.title: Free tier
available.description: The first 50GB you pledge to buddies is free, no card required, including 10GB a month of relay bandwidth for connections that can't go direct. Direct and local-network transfers are always free and unlimited.

available.title: Paid plan and relay bandwidth billing
available.description: Past 50GB, a flat $3 a month for any pledge size. It includes the same 10GB a month of relay bandwidth; relay past that (only when a direct connection isn't possible) is metered at $0.02/GB and shown as its own line item on your invoice, confirmed end to end against real billing.

available.title: Low-disk protection
available.description: Your device refuses incoming files once its own disk runs low (a flat 2GB, or 5% of the disk, whichever's bigger), independent of pledge size, so a buddy's data can never fill your disk to nothing.

available.title: Password reset and account support
available.description: Forgot your password? Use “Forgot password?” on the login page to get a reset link by email. For account, login, billing, or backup questions, use “Contact support” on your dashboard (it sends your account details along, so there's less back-and-forth), or email support@filegarden.net from your account's email address if you can't log in. Resetting your website password never affects your backups: files are encrypted with the passphrase on your own device, which is separate from your account password. That also means nobody, including us, can recover that passphrase if it's lost, so keep it somewhere safe.

available.title: Exclude files and folders
available.description: Client 0.10.0 skips poor fits by default (Outlook PST/OST, live database files, virtual machine disks, temp files and OS clutter), and you can exclude anything else with Syncthing-style patterns in excludes.txt in the client's config folder, or from the Exclusions card on the local dashboard. Edits apply on the next check, no restart needed.

available.title: Local dashboard login
available.description: Client 0.11 puts the local status dashboard behind a login. Set DASHBOARD_PASSWORD in the client's .env for the first login, then change the password from the dashboard whenever you like.

available.title: Activity log on the local dashboard
available.description: Client 0.13 adds an Activity card under your buddies: the last 50 things that happened, in plain language. Files sent or removed (click for the list), a buddy going offline and coming back, files a buddy refused, what a buddy stored with you, restores, exclude-list changes, logins and wrong passwords. Filter to Backups, Problems or Security, or open the raw log for the full detail.

available.title: Warning for big files that keep re-sending
available.description: Any change re-sends the whole file, so a big file that changes often adds up fast. Since client 0.12, the local dashboard lists files re-sent 3 or more times (1 GB or more) in the past week, with a one-click Exclude.

limitations.title: Direct connections aren't guaranteed on every network
limitations.description: Whether a direct connection is possible depends on your router/network's NAT behavior. Many home networks and local networks work great. Some networks (strict corporate firewalls especially) block the hole-punching direct connections need entirely, forwarded port or not. When that happens, your backups still complete normally through our relay; this is expected, graceful behavior, not a failure.

limitations.title: Long transfers can occasionally drop on a local network
limitations.description: Between two buddies on the same local network (or two clients on the same machine), a long transfer can sometimes lose its connection partway through, usually minutes in. Nothing is lost: files of 256 MB or more carry on from where they stopped on the next check, about 30 seconds later, and smaller files are simply sent again. It mostly costs a little time. We're still tracking down the cause.

limitations.title: Every buddy gets the same folder
limitations.description: With more than one buddy, your whole backup folder goes to each of them; you can't send different folders to different buddies yet. Each extra buddy means another full upload, more re-sends of changed files, and more relay bandwidth when a direct connection isn't possible. Buddies are backed up one after another, not all at once.
